newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium hits 2-1/2 month high over $1,500.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium hits 2-1/2 month high over $1,500.

text.p: Three month aluminium futures on the London Metal Exchange (LME) rose above $1,500 a tonne for the first time in 2-1/2 months early on Wednesday, driven higher by chart-related buying.
At 1030 GMT aluminium was bid at $1,502 a tonne, $38 higher than the afternoon kerb close on Tuesday. The next upside chart target was pegged at $1,520, traders said.
On Tuesday aluminium rose above a long-term downtrend and the 100-day moving average, sparking a buying flurry from the speculative community, traders said.
Forward buying of futures and options in 1997 and 1998 as well as a slight tightening in the cash/threes spread, also buoyed the market, they added.

At around 1100 GMT the International Primary Aluminium Institute is due to release average daily aluminium production data for October, which some traders are expecting to show a slight decline from September levels of 50,800 tonnes.
